author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose controller buttons that activate twice
summary: Use a neutral input display to distinguish duplicate emulator bindings, two Android device interfaces, turbo mode, accessibility actions, and game repeat behavior, changing one layer until one press creates one transition.
heroAlt: PCSX2 pad test window showing individual DualShock inputs and live axis values

sourceLabels.android-game-controller: Android controller events, axes, and device behavior

blocks.text: Count raw transitions outside the affected game

A menu skipping two entries can come from two bindings on one port, one controller exposed as both gamepad and keyboard, turbo or macro mode, an Android accessibility shortcut, or the game's own key-repeat behavior. Begin in an input test that displays individual PS2 controls. Press and release once without moving other controls and record which indicators change and whether they remain held.
Do not clear every controller and touchscreen profile at once. Preserve the working layout and isolate the duplicated path so unrelated controls remain recoverable.

items: Current controller mapping exported or captured.
One physical controller connected and touchscreen input idle.
Turbo, macro, and mode switches located on the device instructions.
An emulator input-test view plus the affected game menu.
Android accessibility and key-remapping services documented.

blocks.text: Remove duplicate input paths one at a time

items: 1. Press the affected button once in the neutral test and record every active PS2 control.
2. Inspect that PS2 function for multiple physical binding entries.
3. Check whether the same device appears as both controller and keyboard source.
4. Disable turbo or macro mode using the documented device procedure.
5. Pause third-party key remappers for one controlled pass.
6. Test with touchscreen overlay hidden but do not delete its profile.
7. Return to the game and distinguish immediate double activation from held-key repeat.
8. Reconnect and confirm one press still produces one press and one release.

blocks.text: The neutral display distinguishes a duplicated raw event from game logic. If two PS2 controls illuminate together, the mapping is wrong; if one control flickers rapidly, turbo is likely; if the neutral test is correct but one menu repeats, the title's repeat threshold or a stuck axis deserves separate investigation.
The fix passes only when press and release counts remain correct in both the tester and the original game.

items: One physical press activates one PS2 control.
The control returns fully to neutral on release.
No second logical device feeds the same port.
Turbo and macros are in their intended state.
The result survives reconnection and app restart.
A stick axis rests beyond dead zone: follow stuck-axis diagnosis.
Only one game menu repeats held input: test title-specific behavior.
Two controllers share Port 1: separate device assignments.
A system shortcut still fires: inspect Android accessibility or remapping settings.

blocks.text: Restore the exported mapping if isolation fails

Import the original profile, restore deliberately disabled accessibility services, return the controller to its documented normal mode, and reconnect once. Keep the one-press table to guide the next layer without destructive resets.
Bluetooth retransmission is not usually a clean double press

Radio interference more often causes delay, loss, or bursts than perfectly repeatable duplicate mappings. Prove the raw transition pattern before blaming wireless transport. Compare a single tap, a held press, and release in the neutral tester; a second mapped source usually produces two named activations, while turbo produces a rapid series and game key-repeat appears only after a hold. Preserve that distinction so the fix removes the responsible binding instead of weakening responsiveness globally.
